finding: The Deskstar 25GP and 22GXP are separately identified capacity and rotation-speed variants; not duplicate records.
source_evidence: Reuters identifies the 25 GB 5400 RPM 25GP and the 22 GB 7200 RPM 22GXP separately in IBM's November 1998 unveiling.
recommended_next_action: Retain separate frozen records; obtain ordering identifiers only if later normalization requires SKU-level identity.

finding: Fireball EL and Fireball EX are different named HDD families but the frozen records are family-level rather than per-capacity SKU records; their capacities must not be retroactively treated as separate candidates without a new scoped scout run.
source_evidence: Quantum reports the Fireball EL and EX as named new products and gives family-level production timing rather than a complete per-SKU launch register.
recommended_next_action: Keep each as a family-level frozen record; require separate evidence and a declared granularity decision before any SKU expansion.

finding: The Q1 1999 distributor and reseller availability statement must not be inherited into either Deskstar record as a 1998 broad-channel launch date. The only stated 1998 availability is limited shipment to PC makers for Christmas.
source_evidence: Reuters distinguishes limited 1998 PC-maker shipments from distributor and reseller availability in the first quarter of 1999.
recommended_next_action: Preserve two event facts in any later review: November 11 unveiling and limited 1998 OEM shipment; do not infer a 1998 retail-channel date.

finding: May 1998 mass production and planned May availability do not independently establish a first commercial shipment or an exact introduction date for Fireball EL.
source_evidence: The contemporary report describes planned May availability; the associated Quantum filing establishes May mass production but not a dated commercial shipment.
recommended_next_action: Keep the record at human review and seek a dated OEM or distribution shipment source before treating mass production as the qualifying commercial event.

finding: Fireball EX has a dated June 8 announcement and July mass production; the frozen evidence does not state a precise first commercial shipment or channel geography.
source_evidence: The report gives the June 8 announcement and says the series would enter mass production in July; it does not document a day of commercial availability.
recommended_next_action: Retain the dated announcement separately from production timing and seek OEM or distribution shipment evidence if the cohort rule requires commercial shipment.

finding: The four-record bounded pilot covers only Quantum and IBM desktop/workstation fixed HDDs. It is not an all-manufacturer or all-segment 1998 HDD cohort; desktop competitors and SCSI enterprise/mobile and other segments require a declared stopping rule and separate scout coverage.
source_evidence: The contemporary report documents 1998 Seagate enterprise SCSI introductions alongside the pilot's desktop-focused records; showing that segment coverage is intentionally incomplete.
recommended_next_action: Keep the present sample labeled bounded; open separately sourced omission leads without adding any entities to this audit run.

finding: Maxtor DiamondMax 2880 is an omission lead: a February 24 1998 announcement described a new 3.5-inch UltraDMA/33 family with mass-production shipment planned from March. It is not added as a candidate here.
source_evidence: Contemporary reporting says Maxtor announced the DiamondMax 2880 on February 24 and planned mass-production shipping from March.
recommended_next_action: Create a separate scout lead for product identity and actual commercial-shipment evidence; do not treat the forecast shipment as verified availability.

finding: Seagate Barracuda 18LP family is an omission lead: the October 1998 announcement included Barracuda 18LP products and stated November 1998 mass shipment for the series except the 50 GB configuration. It is not added as a candidate here.
source_evidence: The report lists Barracuda 18LP 9/18/36/50 GB models and states November mass shipment except for the 50 GB model in March 1999.
recommended_next_action: Create a scoped enterprise-SCSI scout record at family or clearly separated model granularity; verify commercial channel and do not assign November timing to the 50 GB configuration.

finding: Seagate Cheetah 18LP is a boundary-control lead rather than evidence of 1998 commercial inclusion: it was announced in October 1998 but the cited report gives February 1999 mass shipment.
source_evidence: The report lists Cheetah 18LP products in the 1998 announcement and says mass shipment would start in February 1999.
recommended_next_action: Record it only as a prospective lead; exclude it from a 1998 shipment-qualified cohort unless independent evidence establishes an earlier qualifying event under the declared rule.

finding: Western Digital WD Expert is a provisional omission lead: a December 1998 contemporary report calls it a new 7200 RPM drive; the available evidence does not establish a primary-source launch date or first commercial shipment.
source_evidence: EDN describes WD Expert as a new 7200 RPM drive and reports that it was shipping ahead of schedule; the article alone is insufficient for a precise cohort event.
recommended_next_action: Seek a dated Western Digital press release or regulatory filing and independently verify product identity and shipment timing before a new scout candidate is considered.

finding: IBM Microdrive is a provisional omission lead with an event ambiguity: IBM's 1998 annual report says Microdrive debuted in September; the pilot has no evidence for 1998 commercial shipment. A debut or presentation must not be converted into a shipment fact.
source_evidence: IBM states that Microdrive debuted in September but does not in this statement give a commercial shipment date or channel.
recommended_next_action: Find the original IBM announcement and contemporaneous availability evidence; classify announcement or presentation separately from first commercial shipment before any scout candidate is proposed.
